33182.subject: English Language

33187.subject: English Language

33190.subject: English Language

In the sentence below, there is one underlined word and one gap. From the list of words lettered A to D, choose the one that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word and that will, at the same time correctly fill the gap in the sentence.

33190.explanation:
Brevity;  concise and exact use of words in writing or speech. shortness 

verbosity; the fact or quality of using more words than needed; wordiness.

33192.subject: English Language
33192.question_text:
In the sentence below, there is one underlined word and one gap. From the list of words lettered A to D, choose the one that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word and that will, at the same time correctly fill the gap in the sentence.

33192.explanation:
Accidentally; by chance; inadvertently

Deliberately; consciously and intentionally; on purpose.

33195.subject: English Language
33195.question_text:
In the sentence below, there is one underlined word and one gap. From the list of words lettered A to D, choose the one that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word and that will, at the same time correctly fill the gap in the sentence.

compulsory; required by law or a rule; obligatory.

optional; available to be chosen but not obligatory.

33200.subject: English Language
33200.question_text:
In the sentence below, there is one underlined word and one gap. From the list of words lettered A to D, choose the one that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word and that will, at the same time correctly fill the gap in the sentence.

The Magistrate convicted the hardened criminal but .....and discharged the first offender
33200.explanation:
convicted; having been declared guilty of a criminal offence by the verdict of a jury or the decision of a judge.

Acquitted; free (someone) from a criminal charge by a verdict of not guilty.

33203.subject: English Language
33203.question_text:
In the sentence below, there is one underlined word and one gap. From the list of words lettered A to D, choose the one that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word and that will, at the same time correctly fill the gap in the sentence.

33203.explanation:
sturdy;  strongly and solidly built.

fragile; easily broken or damaged.

33207.subject: English Language
33207.question_text:
In the sentence below, there is one underlined word and one gap. From the list of words lettered A to D, choose the one that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word and that will, at the same time correctly fill the gap in the sentence.

33207.explanation:
Strict; demanding that rules concerning behaviour are obeyed and observed.

Lenient; more merciful or tolerant than expected.

33209.subject: English Language
33209.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

The brutal killing of members of the opposition provoked strong ......
33209.explanation:
condemnation; the expression of very strong disapproval; censure.

The brutal killing of members of the opposition provoked strong condemnation

33217.subject: English Language
33217.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

The doctor ....... my illness as malaria
33217.explanation:
Diagnosed; identify the nature of (an illness or other problem) by examination of the symptoms.

The doctor diagnosed my illness as malaria

33220.subject: English Language
33220.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

Since we should not disclose our identity, our letter to the principal must be .....
33220.explanation:
Anonymous; (of a person) not identified by name; of unknown name.

Since we should not disclose our identity, our letter to the principal must be anonymous

33222.subject: English Language
33222.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

Although we pleaded for long with our father, he remained ....... that we should not go to the stadium.
33222.explanation:
Adamant; refusing to be persuaded or to change one's mind.

Although we pleaded for long with our father, he remained adamant that we should not go to the stadium.

33224.subject: English Language
33224.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

Since hard drugs are destroying our youths, our government has placed an ....... on them
33224.explanation:
Embargo; impose an official ban on (trade or a country or commodity).

Since hard drugs are destroying our youths, our government has placed an embargo on them

33229.subject: English Language
33229.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

Oseli's ....... teacher teaches English, Physics, Economics and Technical Drawing.
33229.explanation:
versatile; able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities

Oseli's versatile teacher teaches English, Physics, Economics and Technical Drawing.

33232.subject: English Language
33232.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

Some political leaders love ....... who always praise their governments.
33232.explanation:
sycophants; a person who acts obsequiously towards someone important in order to gain advantage. Flatterers, praise-singers

Some political leaders love sycophants who always praise their governments.

33234.subject: English Language
33234.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

The ....... of the new king will take place next week
33234.explanation:
coronation; the ceremony of crowning a sovereign or a sovereign's consort, king

The coronation of the new king will take place next week

33235.subject: English Language
33235.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

The match was a ..... for Brazil because their team was stronger than the opposing team.
33235.explanation:
Walkover; an easy victory.

The match was a walkover for Brazil because their team was stronger than the opposing team.

33237.subject: English Language
33237.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that best completes the sentence below.

Kofi is too ....... ; he wants to know about everybody's business
33237.explanation: Inquisitive; to be unduly curious about the affairs of others; prying.

33245.subject: English Language
33245.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

Ali does not let grass grow under his feet. This means that Ali

33247.subject: English Language
33247.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

The dishonest trader always palms off faulty goods on her customers. This means that
33247.explanation: This means the trader sells out or disposes goods usually by trickery or guile to her customers.

options.text: tricks her customers into accepting bad products
pays the penalty for selling faulty goods

33250.subject: English Language
33250.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

Ojo's learning has gone to his head. This means that Ojo
33250.explanation: If something that you have achieved goes to your head, it makes you too proud

options.text: has become proud because of his learning
has been made mad by his learning
feels that only learning is important

33251.subject: English Language
33251.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

When the vice principal left the school, it became a bedlam. This means that
33251.explanation: It became a scene of madness, chaos or great confusion.

options.text: punctuality was the order of the day
there was noise and confusion in the school

33252.subject: English Language
33252.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

That amount Ivan donated was his widow's mite. This means that Ivan
33252.explanation: A small monetary contribution from someone who is poor.

options.text: gave all that the widow had

33253.subject: English Language
33253.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

Fatou's awkward behavior shows that she is a green horn. This means that Fatou is
33253.explanation: A very young, naïve, immature, or inexperienced person, especially one who is extremely gullible or easily deceived.

33255.subject: English Language
33255.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

To secure more votes, the politician played to the gallery. This means that the politician
33255.explanation:
This means for someone to act in an exaggerated way in order to appeal to popular taste.

To behave in a way intended to make people admire or support you

33257.subject: English Language
33257.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

Those who think that all is well in Cascada are living in a fool's paradise . This means that
33257.explanation: If you say that someone is living in a fool's paradise, you are criticizing them because they are not aware that their present happy situation is likely to change and get worse.

33260.subject: English Language
33260.question_text:
After the sentence below, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for the sentence.

While paying a visit to his uncle, Ayo intends to kill two birds with one stone. This means that Ayo
33260.explanation: The idiom "to kill two birds with one stone" means accomplishing two goals simultaneously. The sentence suggests that while visiting his uncle, Ayo has an additional objective he hopes to achieve during the same visit.

options.text: promises to bring two birds home
takes part in  a double deal
hopes to achieve two aims with one action
intends to do two things at the same time

33262.question_text:

People hardly show their true colors. This means that people rarely show

33268.subject: English Language

From the words lettered A to D below,choose the word or groups of words that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word as it is used in the sentence.

33270.subject: English Language
33270.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D below,choose the word or groups of words that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word as it is used in the sentence.

The team has an arduous task ahead of it.
33270.explanation:
Arduous ;involving or requiring strenuous effort; difficult and tiring.

strenous; requiring or using great effort or exertion.

33272.subject: English Language

From the words lettered A to D below,choose the word or groups of words that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word as it is used in the sentence.

From the words lettered A to D below,choose the word or groups of words that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word as it is used in the sentence.

33273.explanation: Review ; a formal assessment of something with the intention of instituting change if necessary.

33275.subject: English Language
33275.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D below,choose the word or groups of words that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word as it is used in the sentence.

Marian does not have the stamina to run that race.
33275.explanation:
stamina; the ability to sustain prolonged physical or mental effort..

synonyms; energy, vigour, perseverance, strength.

33277.subject: English Language
33277.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

I want just ...... sugar in my tea.
33277.explanation:
A little; a small amount of something.

I want just a little sugar in my tea.

33278.subject: English Language
33278.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Since the opposing parties could not come to an agreement, the peace talks .......
33278.explanation:
Broke down means to fail to function; cease to be useful, effective

Since the opposing parties could not come to an agreement, the peace talks broke down

33280.subject: English Language
33280.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Children often have implicit confidence ....... their parents.
33280.explanation:
'' confidence in'' is used for indicating ones trust in a person, a group of persons, or a procedure.

Children often have implicit confidence in their parents.

33281.subject: English Language
33281.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

If i had heard the news earlier, I ...... stayed at home.
33281.explanation:
When you see "would have" in a sentence it means that the action didn't actually happen, because something else didn't happen first.

The speaker didn't stay at home (first action) because she didn't hear the news (second action)

33283.subject: English Language
33283.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The order is that everyone must be ....... bed by midnight.
33283.explanation:
“In bed” means that you are not just on your bed but also very much ready to sleep. It implies that you are under under the sheets.

"On the bed" means "on the surface" of the bed. The person or object is not under any covering. With "on," there is always an article, or a possessive, or other determiner. "On" never appears alone with "bed."

33284.subject: English Language
33284.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D,
choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

To succeed in any business, one must be prepared to shake ....... one's lazy habits.
33284.explanation:
If you shake off something that you do not want such as an illness or a bad habit, you manage to recover from it or get rid of it.

To succeed in any business, one must be prepared to shake off one's lazy habits.

33285.subject: English Language
33285.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

......... in his right senses will swallow live coals.
33285.explanation: No one  in his right senses will swallow live coals.

33287.subject: English Language
33287.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

One of the clever pupils .....able to solve the problem.
33287.explanation:
''was" is used for things that could have happened in the past or now and correctly fills the gap

One of the clever pupils was able to solve the problem.

33288.subject: English Language
33288.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

He has stopped being foolish .........?
33288.explanation:
Question tags turn a statement into a question. They are often used for checking information that we think we know is true. Usually if the main clause is positive, the question tag is negative, and if the main clause is negative, the question tag is positive.

He has stopped being foolish, (Positive) hasn't he?(negative)

33289.subject: English Language
33289.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

I maintain that the property in question is ......
33289.explanation:
Mine; is used to refer to a thing or things belonging to or associated with the speaker.

I maintain that the property in question is mine.

33291.subject: English Language
33291.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Although Sylvester and John promised to be here, ...... has turned up.
33291.explanation:
Neither means that, not the one nor the other of two people or things; not either.

Although Sylvester and John promised to be here, neither has turned up.

33293.subject: English Language
33293.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The house ....... he lives is spacious.
33293.explanation: In this sentence, the word "where" is used to indicate a location or place. It is commonly used to refer to a place where something or someone is located or resides. In this context, "where" is the most appropriate word to complete the sentence because it specifies the location of the house where the person lives.

33294.subject: English Language
33294.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

It is high time you ...... this place.
33294.explanation: "It's high time (that) we left " means, we are still in the room, but in our mind's eye, we see ourselves in the past, as having already left, and that's why "left" is used. "left" refers to the past, which is where the thoughts are: We should have left before now; We shouldn't have stayed until now.

33296.subject: English Language
33296.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Since you have lost your birth certificate, you have to go ....... an affidavit.
33296.explanation:
Since you have lost your birth certificate, you have to go for an affidavit.

''For'' correctly fills in the gap. To go for something means getting that thing

33297.subject: English Language
33297.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The musicians have not arrived from Sierra Leone, .......?
33297.explanation:
We often use question tags when we expect the listener to agree with our statement. In this case, when the statement is negative, we use a positive question tag. Hence it would read;

The musicians have not arrived from Sierra Leone,(negative) have they? (positive)

33298.subject: English Language
33298.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

On my way home, I saw a ........

33300.explanation: People living in villages have a passion for animals.

33301.subject: English Language
33301.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Kebba and Kwame are very selfish; they care about only .....
33301.explanation: Themselves; used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a group of people or things previously mentioned as the subject of the clause.

33302.subject: English Language
33302.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

You had better ...... your assignment now.
33302.explanation: someone had better something used for saying that someone should do something.

33303.subject: English Language
33303.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Our kind teacher only cautioned the bully and let him.....
33303.explanation:
If you get off with a particular punishment, or if someone gets you off, it means that the punishment could have been much more severe

Our kind teacher only cautioned the bully and let him.off

33305.subject: English Language
33305.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

My .....house is on the next street
33305.explanation: My father-in-law's house is on the next street

33306.subject: English Language
33306.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The Mathematics teacher made us commit the formula ...... memory.
33306.explanation: The Mathematics teacher made us commit the formula to memory.

33308.subject: English Language
33308.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Momodou has been ill ......three weeks now.
33308.explanation: '' for'' is used to specify a period of time.

33309.subject: English Language
33309.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

They kept quiet all the .......
33309.explanation: You use all the while in order to say that something happens continually or that it happens throughout the time when something else is happening.

33310.subject: English Language
33310.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

....... caused the havoc, he sneaked off.
33310.explanation: Having is used with a past participle to form the perfect, pluperfect, and future perfect tenses, and the conditional mood.

33311.subject: English Language
33311.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The point on ....... we disagreed was trivial.
33311.explanation: which is used in referring to something previously mentioned when introducing a clause giving further information.

33313.subject: English Language
33313.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

33313.explanation: Such means of the type or thing previously mentioned.

33326.subject: English Language
33326.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

33330.question_text:

33330.explanation: The phrasal verb “put off” means to postpone or delay. The sentence implies that the decision has already been delayed and can no longer be postponed.

33334.subject: English Language
33334.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The teachers ...... our poor performance in the examinations.
33334.explanation:
Were is used in the second person singular and plural (you, your, yours) and first and third person plural (we, they).

“Discussing” means “talking about (something or someone) with another person or group of people. As a result, if you say, “discussing about” you are being redundant. As a result, the correct sentence would be “They were discussing you.”

33336.subject: English Language
33336.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The wise thing to do is not to give ...... to the temptation.
33336.explanation: Give in ; to cease fighting or arguing; admit defeat.

33340.subject: English Language
33340.question_text:

33340.explanation: That; is used in referring to a specific thing previously mentioned, known, or understood.

33341.subject: English Language
33341.question_text:
From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

The quarrel between Olu and Ola will end up .....a fight.
33341.explanation: ''In'' here is used in expressing the situation of something that is or appears to be enclosed or surrounded by something else. It correctly fills in the gap

33343.subject: English Language

From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.

Musa did not want to fetch water for his grandfather ......, his mother made him do it.

From the words or group of words lettered A to D, choose the word or group of words that best completes the sentence below.
